function: A2C-greedy DRL sets precoding, power loading, beam alignment, combining, splitting ratios, path state information; minimizing transmit power plus CRB under BER, SE, energy limits (pp. 9-10).
system: ULA base station, Mt transmit antennas (25 in figures), users with 2 receive antennas, OTSM-DDAM waveform; 28.65-60 GHz, 700-1760 MHz; no RIS (pp. 4, 11-14).
method: On-policy advantage actor-critic with epsilon-greedy exploration (A2CG), reinforcement learning; actor 3x256 ReLU, critic 2x128; trained online on dataset channels for two users (pp. 10-12, 15).
data_channel: Scenario 1 DeepSense 6G, Scenario 2 highway roadside measurements, Scenario 3 DeepMIMO 5G-NR (Table III); Scenario 3 adds uniform delay and Jakes Doppler shifts (p. 12).
test_conditions: Trained and evaluated within each of three scenarios with two users (Table III); no cross-scenario test stated; compared with perfect path state information (pp. 11-14).
baselines: Learned: A2C, TRPO, DDQN; non-learned: GA-SCA, GA-SCA-ADMM, exhaustive search; perfect path state information; OTSM, OTFS, OFDM waveforms with and without DDAM (pp. 12-15).
metrics: Average reward, BER, SE, CRB, harvested energy, transmitted power, SINR gain, PAPR, objective function, SINR-per-bit loss, complexity order (pp. 12-15).
complexity: A2CG O(Npu GradJ Ntr), same order as A2C; Table IV gives orders of TRPO, DDQN, GA-SCA, GA-SCA-ADMM, exhaustive search; detector O(MN+M^2N^2) (pp. 13, 15).
openness: No code released; public datasets DeepSense 6G, DeepMIMO and 28 GHz V2I highway data (IEEE DataPort doi 10.21227/jqmw-4317) are used (pp. 12, 18).
q1_support: p. 11: "We employ the real-world datasets being available in [39] and [40] for Scenarios 1 and 2"; p. 12: "the adopted training DeepMIMO 5G-NR dataset [41]". Table III (p. 12) names DeepSense 6G, Highway/Roadside and DeepMIMO 5G-NR: measured data and public ray tracing.
q2_support: p. 12: "we evaluate the effectiveness and robustness of the A2CG algorithm under different scenarios listed in Table III". Not met: each scenario is trained and evaluated with its own parameters (Fig. 6), no model trained in one scenario or dataset is tested in another; p. 15: "A2CG, with its adaptive policy, can generalize across channel realizations" is a claim without a test.
q3_support: p. 12: "the convergence speed and reward of the A2CG algorithm are much faster and higher than those of the A2C and TRPO algorithms" (DDQN does not converge); p. 15: "GA-SCA-ADMM shows a performance gap of 20%, 22.3%, and 23.9% at an SINR of 28 dB". Learned baselines are compared on average reward (Fig. 5a), non-learned ones on the objective function (Fig. 11).
q4_support: p. 15: "A2CG, with faster convergence than A2C, maintains the same complexity order" O(Npu GradJ Ntr), with the orders of the other methods in Table IV.
q5_support: p. 12: "the adopted training DeepMIMO 5G-NR dataset [41]", and Table III lists DeepSense 6G Scenario 3; p. 18: "DeepSense 6G: A large-scale real-world multimodal sensing and communication dataset". Public datasets are used; the authors give no link to their own code.
notes: Area 5: the DRL optimizes the ISCAP waveform (precoding, power loading, beam alignment, combining, splitting ratios). Area 4 was considered because the waveform is OTSM-DDAM for high mobility and path state information (delays, Dopplers, gains, angles) is part of the action, but no estimation error is reported and the VAMP-EM detector is not learned (p. 7). In-text dataset citations [39]-[41] (p. 11) do not match the reference list; Table III names DeepSense 6G, Highway/Roadside and DeepMIMO 5G-NR, and refs [43]-[45] (p. 18) are the DeepSense 6G, 28 GHz V2I highway and DeepMIMO datasets. q3 is a judgement: A2C, TRPO and DDQN are compared through average-reward curves (Fig. 5a) and a complexity table, not through BER or CRB, and A2C is also an ablation of A2CG (no greedy step); reviewer to confirm.
